answer: Based on FY2022 data, CVS Health is generally not considered highly capital-intensive. In FY2022, CVS reported total revenues of $322,467 million and capital expenditures (payments to acquire property, plant, and equipment) of $2,727 million, representing a capex-to-revenue ratio of approximately 0.85%. Additionally, its net property, plant, and equipment of $12,873 million represented about 5.64% of total assets of $228,275 million.
rationale: The computed capex-to-revenue ratio (0.85%) and net PPE-to-total-assets ratio (5.64%) demonstrate that CVS Health has relatively low capital intensity relative to its massive scale of operations and total asset base in FY2022.
